title: Caffeine Shift: Runbook Notes and Triage Mosaic (2027-04-11)
content:
Purpose:
This note was composed during the evening on-call ("caffeine" shift) to capture handoff context, short-term mitigations, and runbook edits we discovered were necessary while triaging the two latency incidents on 2027-04-11. Treat as a working doc: quick sketches, hypotheses, and TODOs.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Two distinct-but-related latency degradations observed between 18:10-20:45 UTC.
  1) 18:10–18:34 UTC: a burst of 500–2kms p99 token latencies for request-router->serving-runtime path in us-west-2. Root cause: simultaneous large KV cache misses + autoscaler cooldown not reacting to spool of bursty short-sequence requests.
  2) 19:05–20:40 UTC: a follow-up elevated tail caused by noisy neighbor GPU thermal throttling on a dedicated pool (dedicated-pool-b). Mitigation: move 15% of traffic to dedicated-pool-c and activate model-variant fallback to small-llm-v2 for affected routes.

Incident 1 — bursty KV-miss + autoscaler coupling (18:10–18:34 UTC)
- Trigger: paged alert (SRE-LAT-PR-1) at 18:16. Observed p50 normal, p95+ increased, p99 hit 3.2s generation time for mid-sized prompts (512 tokens).
- Symptoms: sudden increase in requests that cannot use prefix/KV cache; high goroutine count on request-router; batch size dropped to 1–2 for many requests which increased per-token overhead.
- Immediate action taken:
  * 18:17 — routed non-critical traffic to cheaper pool (burst-fallback-policy) to preserve capacity for critical routes.
  * 18:20 — increased request-router cache TTL temporarily (from 30s to 60s) as a soft mitigation to reduce churn while we probed root cause.
  * 18:24 — opened JIRA-INC-3421 to track.
- Root cause hypothesis: a client-side workload (customer X) performed a traffic pattern change causing many cold prefixes; autoscaler cooldown (default 120s) prevented new workers from spinning up fast enough because CPU heuristic required sustained CPU > 60% for scale-up. Autoscaler relies on 60s window which is too long for these bursty short-request patterns.
- Runbook edits suggested:
  * Add a cookbook section: "Handling bursty cold-prefix traffic" with steps: temporary traffic routing, TTL tweak, manual scale-up knob, and re-balance to alternate pools.
  * Expose an autoscaler fast-path flag for on-call: allow immediate +1 worker for extreme tail events (safety TTL 30s).

Incident 2 — noisy neighbor GPU thermal + fallback (19:05–20:40 UTC)
- Trigger: persistent GPU temperature warnings in telemetry on dedicated-pool-b; coincident p99 token latencies rose to ~4.1s for some long-running sequences.
- Symptoms: one host in the pool showed multiple NVLINK retry logs; batch packing degraded as GPUs intermittently dropped fast-path kernels and fell back to a slower kernel variant.
- Immediate action taken:
  * 19:12 — drained traffic off the offending host (host-rtb-07) and quarantined it for hardware ops.
  * 19:30 — bumped routing weight: dedicated-pool-c + hosted-fallback to absorb load.
  * 19:45 — enabled model-variant fallback for customer-tier "beta": small-llm-v2 (quantized) for non-strict-latency routes.
- Follow-up: hardware team issued a support RMA for host-rtb-07; telemetry engineering to add GPU thermal claptrap alerting threshold refinement.

SLO snapshot and notes:
- Request-router p99 target: 3000ms; observed today peak 4100ms during second event.
- Model-serving end-to-end p95 target: 1200ms; hit 1800ms in the first incident.
- Error budget burn: approx 0.27% for request-router p99 during the week (still within monthly budget but trending up).
- Action: schedule a dedicated SLO review during next ops sync to revisit autoscaler percentile windows (proposal: use 95th percentile of short-sequence arrival rate to trigger a fast scale). Owner: Marco Li.

On-call handoff notes (to morning team / next shift):
- Current state: all critical hosts rebalanced; host-rtb-07 quarantined; autoscaler cooldown unchanged (120s). Temporary KV cache TTL bumped back to 30s at 22:00 once traffic normalized.
- Open items for next shift:
  * Confirm RMA progress for host-rtb-07 with HW team (Sana). Jira: JIRA-ENG-7890.
  * Implement autoscaler fast-path flag prototype in a feature branch and run load tests (Ethan). Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/514.
  * Add a short-scope synthetic test that simulates bursty cold-prefix traffic and measure scale-up latency (owner: Aisha).
  * Add a Grafana panel that cross-plots KV-miss rate vs p99 latency for the last 7 days.

Runbook and tooling edits (work items) — PRIORITY: high/medium/low
- High: Add "burst-cold-prefix" cookbook + actionable mitigations (owner: Aisha) — PR for runbook edits: target 2027-04-15.
- High: Add autoscaler quick-unlock flag and guardrail (owner: Marco) — prototype by 2027-04-20.
- Medium: GPU thermal alert refinement, add per-host NVLINK retry count to alert payloads (owner: Sana) — ticketed.
- Medium: Model-variant fallback checklist: ensure fallback telemetry emits a synthetic quality metric and that fallbacks are visible in Console (owner: Product-Host API).
- Low: Investigate whether KV cache TTL heuristics can be learned from traffic (ML-assisted heuristics).

Operational hypotheses and notes (for postmortem if we go that route)
- Hypothesis A: The two incidents share coupling via capacity and routing: the initial KV-miss burst forced a redistribution which pushed more load to dedicated-pool-b, exposing the noisy-neighbor.
- Hypothesis B: Autoscaler heuristics are tuned for steady-state rather than bursty microbursts; adding a short-window sensitivity will reduce tail-burn but risks over-provisioning. Need economic analysis.

Quick commands & artifacts used during triage (copyable):
- Check hot-gpu hosts: ./scripts/pool-health.sh --pool dedicated-pool-b --metric nvlink_retries
- Rebalance route: infra-cli route weight set --route /api/generate --pool dedicated-pool-c --weight 0.25
- TTL tweak: redis-cli -h cache-prod config set prefix_ttl 60

Notes to self / brain-dump (messy):
- We should treat small bursts differently: if 90% of the burst are < 200 tokens then prefer fast scale-up over TTL fiddling.
- Look at client X's recent SDK update (Slack thread #client-x-sdk) — could be batching changes causing cold prefixes. Ping SE for context.
- Could a caching-layer shard rebalancer be starving certain prefixes? Look into the prefix assignment algorithm.

Meeting / handoff prep for 2027-04-12 morning ops sync:
- Agenda items (10m each):
  1) Walk the two incidents and timeline (owner: Aisha)
  2) Proposed autoscaler fast-path change + guardrails (owner: Marco)
  3) GPU thermal and NVLINK alert refinement (owner: Sana)
  4) Runbook PR and priority list (owner: Aisha)
- Prep: attach synthetic trace snippets and p99/p95 charts to the Confluence incident stub.

Appendix (data snippets observed during event):
- KV miss rate spike: baseline 4% -> event peak 38% (18:12)
